# registry_replication_peer (Resource)

One geo-replication partner of this site: where to pull its journal from, and where to forward publishes for feeds homed there.

Credentials are referenced by file path, never inlined: a peer token belongs in a mounted secret, not in Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The EU site: its journal is pulled from the internal listener, and
# publishes for feeds homed there are forwarded to its public URL.
#
# The credential is a file the registry reads, never a value in state.
resource "registry_replication_peer" "eu" {
  name          = "eu"
  url           = "https://eu-internal.example.com:9443"
  public_url    = "https://eu.example.com"
  pull_interval = "2s"
  token_file    = "/etc/fondaco/peers/eu.token"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Peer site name. It must match the name that site calls itself, because it is what feeds refer to in `publish_policy = "forward:<site>"`.
- `url` (String) The peer's internal replication API — the listener that carries the journal, never the public one.

### Optional

- `public_url` (String) The peer's client-facing base URL. Required if any feed here is homed at this peer, because that is where its publishes are forwarded.
- `pull_interval` (String) How often to poll this peer's journal, e.g. `2s`.
- `token_file` (String) Path to the file holding the credential presented to this peer (bearer mode). The registry reads it; Terraform never sees its contents.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The peer name, which is its identity.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Peers are imported by name.
terraform import registry_replication_peer.eu eu
```
